title: Join, Every Tongue, to Praise the Lord
description: Join, Every Tongue, to Praise the Lord in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER NEW, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 883 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Goodness of God Celebrated”, where the book credits them to the Presbyterian Collection.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to WINCHESTER NEW; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Join, ev-ery tongue, to praise the Lord; All na-ture rests up-on his word; Mer-cy and truth his courts main-tain, And own his u-ni-ver-sal reign.

lines: Join, every tongue, to praise the Lord;
All nature rests upon his word;
Mercy and truth his courts maintain,
Seasons and times obey his voice;
The evening and the morn rejoice
To see the earth made soft with showers,
Enriched with fruit, and dressed in flowers.
Thy works pronounce thy power divine;
In all the earth thy glories shine;
Through every month thy gifts appear;
Great God, thy goodness crowns the year.

licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1853.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to WINCHESTER NEW by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
